summary: Build digital service resilience with SRE, chaos engineering, risk mapping, and incident response. Develop practical outputs in this five-day course.
lede: Resilience Engineering for Digital Services connects risk treatment, continuity planning, Site Reliability Engineering, failure mode analysis, and chaos engineering to the technical decisions behind critical digital services. You will learn to identify cloud-native failure modes, map dependencies, assess business impact, test recovery controls, and report resilience performance. Practical work includes building risk registers, calculating service-level indicators, setting error budgets, designing telemetry and dashboards, drafting recovery playbooks, and planning cross-functional game days. You will also explore incident command, graceful degradation, safe chaos experiments, and residual operational risk, with overview-level coverage of automated remediation, AI-assisted anomaly detection, and large-scale resilience testing.
audienceIntro: This digital service resilience course suits professionals who connect technology operations, risk governance, continuity planning, and customer-facing service commitments. It is especially relevant when you need to make reliability trade-offs visible to executives and actionable for engineering teams.
audience: Service Managers using ITIL practices to improve
modules: Cloud Failure Modes and Risk Mapping
prerequisites: You should have practical exposure to IT operations, cloud services, software delivery, business continuity, technology risk, or digital product ownership. Familiarity with distributed systems, incident tickets, service-level reporting, or recovery plans will help, but you do not need to be an SRE or cloud engineer. No programming is required for completion. Exercises use architecture diagrams, structured datasets, dashboards, and templates rather than code development. Advanced topics such as AI-assisted anomaly detection and automated remediation receive conceptual awareness and operational application treatment, while SRE controls, risk mapping, incident playbooks, and game day design receive hands-on application.
